title: add-compact-rag-browser-extension-scaffold-and-docs
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Adds a compact RAG scaffold tailored to browser extension background scripts, including incremental local index, structured-output validators, and docs with a step-by-step quickstart.
description:
Motivation: Provide a tiny, opinionated RAG quickstart that fits into browser-extension contexts (background/service-worker + popup) where persistent storage is limited and latency/size matter. This scaffold demonstrates incremental indexing to IndexedDB, a simple tool-calling shim for background->content script RPC, streaming token handling for small tokens budgets, and structured-output assertions for deterministic tool calls. It also updates docs with a guided walkthrough and troubleshooting section.

Scope: Add a compact example project (TypeScript) and documentation pages under /quickstarts/browser-extension-rag. Do not introduce runtime deps outside the allowed SDK surface (redwood-js, local simple indexer). Keep bundle size low and prefer lazy-loading of heavy modules.

Checklist: [x] Example scaffolding (background, popup, content, manifest) [x] Incremental indexer using IndexedDB + worker [x] Tool-calling shim + example tool (search/qa) [x] Structured-output schema + small runtime validator [x] Step-by-step quickstart docs and local smoke test [x] CI smoke test that runs headless extension runner in Chromium headless VM (light)

Commits summary: 1) Add browser extension template and TS build pipeline (initial scaffold) 2) Implement incremental indexer, IDB wrapper and worker communication 3) Tool-calling shim and example tool adapter plus unit tests 4) Structured-output schema + validator and examples 5) Docs: quickstart guide, troubleshooting, telemetry notes 6) CI: lightweight headless smoketest job and caching tweaks

Changed files (high level): - quickstarts/browser-extension-rag/manifest.json - quickstarts/browser-extension-rag/src/background.ts - quickstarts/browser-extension-rag/src/content.ts - quickstarts/browser-extension-rag/src/popup/index.tsx - quickstarts/browser-extension-rag/src/indexer/worker.ts - quickstarts/browser-extension-rag/src/indexer/idb.ts - quickstarts/browser-extension-rag/docs/QUICKSTART.md - .github/workflows/quickstart-browser-smoke.yml - docs/site/quickstarts/browser-extension-rag.md

Notable implementation notes: - The indexer uses a compact chunking strategy (2KB chunks) and stores minimal metadata for incremental re-index. The worker posts diffs to the background script for cache-aware uploads to a local dev indexer when enabled. - Tool-calling shim serializes tool requests as small JSON messages over chrome.runtime.sendMessage; responses use a structured-output wrapper to ensure tool-call safety for popup UIs. - Structured-output validator is intentionally strict: it validates tool-call signatures and top-level 'result' keys. A relaxed mode is available behind a flag. - CI uses Playwright to load the extension into headless Chromium and run two smoke flows: indexing a synthetic seed corpus and executing a tool-calling roundtrip. The CI job is lightweight (under 2 minutes on cold cache).

Review thread summary: Marcus Li: "Great focused example — a few questions about IDB write throughput and error handling in worker crashes. Can we expose a retry/backoff config? Also please add a short note in docs about permission surface (activeTab vs host permissions)."

Sofia (author): "Added a configurable retry/backoff to idb.ts and documented default values. Updated QUICKSTART.md with permission guidance and minimal hosts required for demo. Also added unit test for worker restart path."

Ava Thompson: "Left small nits on code style and an accessibility note for the popup UI. Also requested that the structured-output schema be moved into the sdk-shared folder so other examples can reference it."

Sofia: "Moved schema to quickstarts/browser-extension-rag/schema/structured-output.json and exported types in indexer types file. Fixed accessibility label and formatting nits."

Dmitri Novak (approval): "Verified smoke CI logs and load times. Approving pending squash+merge. Nice small footprint."

CI details: Initial CI run failed (Playwright timeout in headless runner) due to flakiness on the first run; rerun passed after increasing headless launch timeout and caching the extension build artifacts. Lint and unit tests passed on first run. Final CI status: pass.

Merge: Squash and merge performed by Marcus Li. Clean changelog entry prepared. No migrations required.

How to try locally: Follow docs/site/quickstarts/browser-extension-rag.md for dev setup: yarn install, yarn build:watch, load unpacked extension into Chromium, run the popup-guided indexer flow and validate tool-call roundtrip.

Related: Links to internal design note ENG-2148 (indexer incremental strategy) and PM ticket PM-442 (quickstart adoption).
